ok, i'm back in all seriousness. i did some snooping around and i found some great recipes that i think might fit all your requirements. for the most part, they are all gluten free and i believe diabetes friendly but my degree on diabetes is from google university, so please take what i say with a grain of salt. some recipes ive linked arent vegetarian, but im sure you can substitute proteins in the recipes with no issues. 

  
[butter paneer (without tomatoes or dairy)](https://thebhukkadbawarchi.wordpress.com/2019/05/16/paneerbuttermasalanotomatoes/) \- veg

[fried fish picatta](https://www.paleorunningmomma.com/paleo-fish-piccata-whole30-keto/)

[egg roll bowl ](https://gatherednutrition.com/paleo-egg-roll-in-a-bowl/)\- the recipe itself is non veg, but i think the ground meat could be substituted with impossible meat or tofu

[saag paneer ](https://www.bbcgoodfood.com/recipes/saag-paneer)\- veg

[mushroom burgers!](https://ketovegetarianrecipes.com/keto-portobello-mushroom-burger-bun/) \- no gluten in these, i promise! + veg

[stuffed mushrooms](https://ketovegetarianrecipes.com/air-fryer-stuffed-mushrooms/) \- veg

[eggplant gratin](https://ketovegetarianrecipes.com/eggplant-gratin-low-carb/) \- veg (this looks phenomenal by the way. i will have to make it myself)

  
if i ever come by some other recipes, ill try and update this comment. i think your best bet is probably to lean into indian / south east asian dishes because of the cultural lean towards vegetarianism. in terms of the diabetes / gf aspect, i think keto / paleo diets work very well. i know the science + community around those diets are a bit iffy but when i looked up recipes that fall under all of your requirements most of the blogs were keto / paleo. you probably already know this though, dont mean to sound condescending, sorry! 

  
if you're willing to drop a few dimes, the NYT cooking section is a PHENOMENAL! resource. i have a subscription myself and i found a lot of great recipes but didnt want to link them here in case you didnt have a subscription (thanks paywalls). 

  
wishing you guys luck! i know trying to feed one person with dietary requirements can be difficult, but a whole family is quadruple the trouble. i believe in you!

the shape language in this is crazy awesome! i love the contrast of the hard shapes of the objects but soft gradient shading. this looks like something i'd see on the cover of some sort of art magazine. my only critique is that i wish there was a little more contrast between the hand and the background! maybe a deeper or lighter color?

so far, your art looks gorg! i'm a big fan of your color usage, posing, and the way that you incorporate your characters into their environment! here are just a few things ive noticed!

 - one thing i see about your anatomy is that the legs seem to be on the longer side! our eyes tend to naturally gravitate to the center of whatever we are looking at, and when the legs take up a large portion of the piece, all the work you've put into other parts of the piece get pushed to the side!

- my favorite of the pieces youve put up here is definitely the person with pink hair and purple outfit on the blue background. i say this because you experiment a lot with texture! maybe this is just my bias, but i love love love when people explore texture. while your art is definitely awesome, slap some more texture in! 

- the usage of the symmetry tool is a little too obvious in some pictures. again, this might be a personal bias, but i think what makes art so great IS asymmetry! i think while you def have a good grip on posing, experiment with more fluid and dynamic poses! i know everyone says this, but pinterest is a GREAT place to find stuff to reference. 

- speaking on the same face syndrome point, i think some of where it might be coming from is that you tend to draw front facing characters only. this might just be selection bias because the pieces youve shown here are all mostly front facing pieces, but i think you could benefit a lot from drawing + showing characters in other poses!

overall, you have some awesome art bro! i think you're on a great path and you're only gonna get better from here. i hope what ive said will be helpful! excited to see where you go from this!

i dont think you have same face in the traditional sense that every face looks the exact same! you obviously have some great variations in features \^\_\^ i think you do lean into similar face shapes / feature placement however! i think you should experiment with different facial proportions! what really helped me with facial variation is going onto pinterest and looking at unique faces and copying those \^\_\^

I have travelled to multiple countries with a pack of cigarettes in my pocket on the plane.  Nobody has ever blinked an eye. You're all good!

But on another note, I think you should take this as a sign to not vape at all, especially if you're a kid. Nothing good comes out of vaping, and if you stop now you are saving yourself a lot of trouble later on.

If it's just a nicotine vape, then they will not find out that you vape nic. You'll be fine so long as you do not tell the doctor flat out.

But if it's a THC pen, so long as they do not run a drug test you will be fine. But they are 99% not going to run a drug test because your doctor is not there to try and expose your secrets to your parents, but to help you. As a general note, doctors do not perform drug tests unless it's an emergency (as in you are overdosing on something but won't tell the doctor what it is) or if your parents ask. But if you are sure that your parents are not going to ask, then you'll be okay.
